title: Page layouts, compact layouts, Lightning record pages, and Dynamic Forms
objectives: Explain a page layout as the organization of fields, buttons, and related lists on a record, including visible, read-only, and required.
Use a compact layout for the highlights-panel / mobile header field set, not as a replacement for the full page layout.
Distinguish a Lightning record page (App Builder region and component assignment) from the page layout it may still host.
Use Dynamic Forms to place fields and sections as App Builder components with visibility rules, reducing layout/record-type sprawl when it fits.
diagnostic_question: Facilities wants different fields for Commercial properties, a short header of Name/City/Owner, and to hide rehab fields unless Status is Rehab. Which of page layout, compact layout, Lightning record page, and Dynamic Forms do you reach for—and which one is not FLS?
definition: A page layout controls the organization of buttons, fields, custom links, and related lists on a record page and helps determine which fields are visible, read only, and required. When record types exist, the user's profile plus the record type determine the page layout. A Lightning record page is an App Builder assignment of regions and components. Dynamic Forms migrate fields and sections from the page layout into individual Lightning App Builder components that can use visibility rules. ([Page Layouts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=customize_layout.htm); [Break Up Your Record Details with Dynamic Forms](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.dynamic_forms_overview.htm); [Create Record Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=creating_record_types.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for four different surfaces. A compact layout is not a page layout. A Lightning page is not FLS. Dynamic Forms can reduce how many page layouts and record types you need, but related lists and some objects still depend on the layout. Hiding a field on a layout does not hide it from the API.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel room. The page layout is the furniture arrangement—desks, closets, which drawers are locked or required. The compact layout is the door-card summary: three facts the hallway shows. The Lightning record page is the floor plan that places the minibar, the TV, and the furniture block as components. Dynamic Forms lets you move dressers without rebuilding the whole suite and hide the ironing board unless the guest is staying for rehab week. The lock on the safe is FLS, not furniture.
deeper_explanation: Page Layouts Help: layouts control buttons, fields, s-controls, Visualforce, custom links, and related lists, and help determine visible, read-only, and required. Assign layouts to profiles; with record types, profile plus record type choose the layout. ([Page Layouts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=customize_layout.htm); [Create Record Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=creating_record_types.htm))

Compact layouts define the short field set used in places such as the highlights panel and mobile header. Exact UI labels are release-sensitive—Needs verification of the current compact-layout Help article title in the target org. They do not replace related lists or the full field arrangement.

Lightning record pages are assigned by app, record type, and profile (assignment model is release-sensitive—confirm in Lightning App Builder). They host components, including a Record Detail component that still reads the page layout until you enable Dynamic Forms.

Dynamic Forms: migrate fields and sections from the page layout to App Builder components; use visibility rules on record data, user details, and device; reduce the number of page layouts and record types; move toward a single Lightning page assignment model instead of always pairing a Lightning page with a page layout. Cross-object fields can be placed from lookup parents. Not every object is Dynamic Forms-enabled by default; some pages migrate, some start enabled. ([Break Up Your Record Details with Dynamic Forms](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.dynamic_forms_overview.htm))

Related lists, some actions, and objects without Dynamic Forms still use the page layout. Layout requiredness is not the field-level Required attribute (DATA-002) and not a validation rule (DATA-010).

mental_model.analogy: A hotel room: page layout is furniture and locked drawers, compact layout is the door-card summary, Lightning record page is the floor plan of components, Dynamic Forms is rearranging furniture with visibility rules, and FLS is the safe lock.
useful_mapping: page layout → furniture arrangement, related-list walls, required/read-only drawers
Lightning record page → floor plan and component placement
Record Detail component → the old furniture block still driven by the page layout
Dynamic Forms → individual dressers you can hide with visibility rules
profile + record type → which room style you get
FLS → the safe, not the furniture
where_it_breaks: Not every object supports Dynamic Forms; do not promise it on every standard object.
Related lists often remain layout-driven even after field migration.
Assignment of Lightning pages vs layouts is a dual model until Dynamic Forms is fully adopted.
Mobile can still honor compact layouts and layouts in ways the hotel analogy simplifies.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Page layouts arrange fields, buttons, and related lists and can mark required or read-only. Compact layouts feed the highlights header. Lightning record pages place components. Dynamic Forms breaks the detail block into visibile sections. None of that is FLS.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I assign layouts by profile and record type. I use a compact layout for Name/City/Owner. I use a Lightning page for component placement. terminology.precise: Organizes buttons, fields, links, and related lists; helps set visible, read-only, and required. Assigned by profile and record type.
terminology.example: Commercial Facilities layout with unit related list.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lightning record page: component floor plan that may still host this layout.

terminology.precise: Defines which fields appear in highlights-style and similar header presentations. Does not arrange related lists.
terminology.example: Name, City, Owner on the property header.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Search layout: another short field set for search results, neighboring.
terminology.boundary: Confirm current surfaces in org Help.

terminology.precise: A Lightning page assigned to an app/record type/profile that hosts components around a record.
terminology.example: Property record page with a chart component beside details.
terminology.non_example: A Visualforce page override from Classic only.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Home page or app page: other Lightning page types.
terminology.boundary: Assignment is separate from page-layout assignment.

terminology.plain: The layout-driven field block on a Lightning page.
terminology.precise: Until Dynamic Forms, fields still come from the page layout inside this component.
terminology.example: Default detail block on a new record page.
terminology.non_example: A Field Section component after migration.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Related List component: lists, not the detail block.
terminology.boundary: Migrating removes dependence on that block for fields.

terminology.precise: Migrate page-layout fields/sections into App Builder; visibility rules; can reduce layouts and record types; cross-object lookup fields supported.
terminology.example: Rehab section visible when Status = Rehab.
terminology.non_example: A new record type created only to hide that section.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Dynamic Actions: action visibility, neighboring DATA-011.

terminology.plain: Show or hide a component from record/user/device data.
terminology.precise: Dynamic Forms lets you show and hide fields and sections using visibility rules.
terminology.non_example: FLS hiding a field from all UI and API.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Filter criteria on a roll-up: different feature.

terminology.precise: Page layouts help determine required fields for that presentation. Distinct from the field Required attribute and from validation rules.
terminology.example: Description required on the Facilities layout only.
terminology.boundary: API loads may skip layout requiredness.

terminology.precise: Page layouts control related lists. Dynamic Forms field migration does not automatically replace every related list.
terminology.example: Units related list on the property layout.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Dynamic related list component: Lightning-page alternative—confirm in App Builder.
terminology.boundary: Still a reason to keep a page layout.

interview_questions.question: Compare page layout, compact layout, Lightning record page, and Dynamic Forms.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Page layout arranges fields, buttons, and related lists. Compact layout feeds the highlights header. Lightning record page places components. Dynamic Forms turns fields and sections into visibile App Builder components. None of them is FLS.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I assign layouts by profile and record type. I use compact layouts for the door card. I use Lightning pages for components. I migrate to Dynamic Forms to cut layout sprawl when the object supports it. I keep related lists in mind. I do not invent object support.
interview_questions.example: Property: compact Name/City/Owner; two Commercial layouts; DF Rehab section.
follow_ups: What still needs a page layout after DF?
Is DF on Case in this org?
weak_answer_warnings: Using one word 'layout' for all four

interview_questions.question: Highlights show the wrong fields after you edited the page layout. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Highlights come from the compact layout (and the highlights component), not from the first fields on the page layout.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open Compact Layouts, put the intended fields in order, and assign the compact layout. I confirm the Lightning page still has a highlights panel. I do not delete body fields to 'fix the header.'
interview_questions.example: Assigned a compact layout with Name, City, Owner; page layout still has twenty fields.
tradeoffs: Highlights component missing vs wrong compact
follow_ups: Does mobile use the same compact layout?
Can each record type have a compact layout?

interview_questions.question: They want a Rehab record type only to hide three fields. Your answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Prefer Dynamic Forms visibility rules if the object supports them. A record type is for process and picklist differences (DATA-008), not a hide.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I ask whether Status already means Rehab. If yes, a visibility rule on the section is enough. I still use a record type if picklists and processes differ. I do not turn off FLS for everyone. I mark DF object support Needs verification if the migrate action is missing.
interview_questions.example: Rejected Rehab record type; Status = Rehab visibility on a Field Section.
follow_ups: What if related lists must also change?

interview_questions.question: Why is a page layout not security?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Layouts help determine what the UI shows as visible, read-only, or required. API users and reports can still access fields allowed by FLS and sharing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I give the salary example. I mention layout read-only versus FLS. I mention Dynamic Forms visibility is also presentation. I point SEC for authorization. I still use layouts to reduce clutter for humans.
interview_questions.example: Salary off every layout but readable in a report for a user with FLS.
follow_ups: Do validation rules fire if the field is not on the layout?
weak_answer_warnings: Promising layouts hide fields from Data Loader

interview_questions.question: Finance and Facilities need different Commercial related lists.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Assign different page layouts to those profiles for the Commercial record type. Dynamic Forms field sections will not replace that related-list need by themselves.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep one Commercial record type if values match. I use the layout assignment matrix. I may also assign different Lightning pages if components differ. I do not clone the Property object.
interview_questions.example: Facilities Commercial layout shows Units; Finance layout shows Vendor pairings only.
tradeoffs: Two layouts vs two Lightning pages
Related list component vs layout related list
follow_ups: Can Dynamic Related Lists replace the layout list?
weak_answer_warnings: A third record type named Finance-Commercial

interview_questions.question: Migrate to Dynamic Forms is not available on the page.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The object or page may not support Dynamic Forms. Confirm current Help for that object. Stay on page layouts and Lightning components until it does.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not invent an edition name. I check I am in Lightning App Builder on a record page. I document the fallback. I do not tell the business we will 'just enable it' without a source.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ custom object offered migration; a standard object in the same org did not—Needs verification per object.
tradeoffs: Wait for support vs extra layouts
follow_ups: Which objects start with DF enabled?
Do save options migrate on Account/Case/Lead?

interview_questions.question: How do Lightning record pages and page layouts work together before Dynamic Forms?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The Lightning page is the floor plan. The Record Detail component still renders the page layout. You assign both: the page and the layout (dual model).
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help says Dynamic Forms moves toward a single Lightning page assignment model. Until then I expect both assignments. Related lists and some actions stay layout-aware. I do not edit only the Lightning page and expect field order to change if Record Detail is still layout-driven.
interview_questions.example: Changed field order on the page layout; Lightning page with Record Detail immediately showed it.
tradeoffs: Dual assignment vs DF single model
Edit layout vs edit Field Section
follow_ups: What assignment dimensions does a Lightning page use?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying Lightning pages replaced layouts entirely in every org

interview_questions.question: Where do cross-object fields fit on a record page?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Dynamic Forms can place lookup-parent fields on the page. A formula field can also display a parent value (DATA-006). A page layout can show that formula. Do not stamp a text copy just to put it on the layout.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I prefer a formula or DF cross-object field so the parent remains the source of truth. I still watch unique-relationship caps if I create a new formula. I do not use a compact layout as the only place a parent field exists if users need it in the body.
interview_questions.example: Property city on Inspection via DF cross-object or a formula, not Inspection.CityStamp__c.
follow_ups: Does DF cross-object count as a unique relationship?
Can compact layouts include formula fields?
weak_answer_warnings: Creating a text stamp for the header only
